needs: The arc-rotate camera always builds its look-at with the constant world up (Vec3Up), whatever the sign of sin(beta), so a negative beta never flips the picture: it stays upright (no Babylon.js allowUpsideDown-style up negation).

needs: With the default limits the camera clamps pitch, on every write to yaw, pitch, radius or center, to an effective maximum that falls from pitchMax at 2x planetRadius to pitchMin (0.001) at 4x (limits.pitchDisabledRadiusScale defaults to {x:2,y:4}). A new camera starts at radiusMax = 4x planetRadius, so assigning camera.pitch alone leaves it looking straight down.

Setting camera.limits.pitchDisabledRadiusScale = null (or pushing its radii out of reach) turns this fade off, so full pitch is allowed at every radius and the tilt survives later radius changes. needs: On its first frame interpolateArcRotateCamera sets all of the camera's inertial offsets to zero before it records the pose, so a camera still coasting from a flick when the call is made does not cancel it, and the await resolves (a).

Once the transition is under way, anything else that changes alpha/beta/radius/target between its frames cancels it and the promise rejects; a user drag through attachControl (directly or through the inertia it adds) is one such change (b).
A second interpolateArcRotateCamera call on the same camera writes the pose too, so the first call's promise rejects while the newer one runs on (c).
